steps: Lie with your eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Grip a little wider than your shoulders, unrack and lower the bar to your mid chest.
Press up and slightly back until your arms are straight over your shoulders.
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides

steps: Set the bench to 30–45°, shoulder blades back, feet flat.
Lower the bar to your upper chest, just under the collarbones.
Press straight up over your shoulders.
mistakes: Bench set too steep (it becomes a shoulder press)
Lifting the hips off the bench

steps: Hook your legs in the pads and lie back with your shoulder blades pulled together.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Letting the bar drift toward the face
Unracking without a spotter on heavy sets

steps: Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, lie back and bring them over your chest.
Lower them to the sides of your chest, elbows about 45° from your body.
Press up and slightly together without banging them.
mistakes: Going too deep and losing tension in the shoulders
Dropping the dumbbells at the end instead of bringing them back to the thighs

steps: Bench at 30–45°, dumbbells over your upper chest.
Lower them to the sides of your upper chest with elbows slightly tucked.
Press up until your arms are straight, wrists stacked over elbows.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears

steps: Lie on a flat bench with the dumbbells over your chest, palms facing each other.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows and open the arms in a wide arc until you feel a stretch.
Bring them back up along the same arc, squeezing the chest.
mistakes: Bending the elbows more and more (it becomes a press)
Going so low it hurts the front of the shoulder

steps: Set the pulleys at shoulder height, step forward with one foot, slight lean.
With soft elbows, bring the handles together in front of your chest in an arc.
Open slowly until your hands are in line with your chest.
mistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of hugging with the chest
Letting the weights yank you back

steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height, back flat on the pad.
Bring the handles together in front of you with a slight bend in the elbows.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch in the chest.
mistakes: Seat too low or too high
Letting the plates touch between reps

steps: Set the seat so the handles are at mid-chest height.
Press forward until your arms are almost straight.
Bring the handles back slowly to just in front of your chest.
mistakes: Lifting the shoulders off the pad

steps: Hands a little wider than your shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest to just above the floor, elbows about 45° from the body.
Push back up keeping the body straight.
Support yourself on the bars with straight arms, lean the torso forward.
Lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Push back up without locking the elbows hard.
mistakes: Going too deep with a sore shoulder
Staying too upright (it shifts to the triceps)

steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Pull your shoulder blades down, then pull until your chin is over the bar.
Lower all the way down under control.
Hang with palms facing you, hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
mistakes: Reaching with the chin instead of pulling with the back

steps: Sit with your thighs under the pad and grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders.
Lean back slightly and pull the bar to your upper chest, elbows down and back.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Swinging the torso to move the weight

steps: Hinge at the hips with a flat back until your torso is about 45° or lower.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs, elbows close to the body.
Lower it under control to straight arms.
mistakes: Standing up more on every rep

steps: One hand and knee on a bench, back flat, dumbbell hanging under the shoulder.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, elbow close to the body.
Lower it until your arm is straight and the shoulder stretches.
mistakes: Twisting the torso to lift it
Pulling toward the chest instead of the hip

steps: Sit tall with feet on the platform and knees slightly bent.
Pull the handle to your belly, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Let the arms extend forward slowly without rounding the back.
Straddle the bar, hinge at the hips with a flat back.
Pull the handle to your chest, elbows back.
Lower under control to straight arms.
mistakes: Using the legs to heave the weight

steps: Set the seat so your chest rests on the pad and you can reach the handles.
Pull the handles back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly until the arms are straight.
mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad

steps: Stand facing a high pulley, arms almost straight, slight forward lean.
Sweep the bar down to your thighs keeping the arms straight.
Let it rise slowly back to eye level.
mistakes: Bending the elbows (it becomes a pushdown)

steps: Set a rope at face height and hold it with thumbs toward you.
Pull the rope toward your face, hands apart, elbows high.
Return slowly to straight arms.
mistakes: Using too much weight and leaning back

steps: Bar over mid-foot, grip just outside the legs, back flat, chest up.
Push the floor away and stand up with the bar close to your legs.
Lower it by pushing the hips back, then bending the knees.
mistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the legs

steps: Set the bar on the pins at or just below knee height.
Grip it, flatten your back and stand up by driving the hips forward.
Lower it back to the pins under control.
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the bar

steps: Set the pad just under your hip bones, body straight.
Bend at the hips and lower your torso with a flat back.
Come back up until your body is in a straight line.
Lie under a bar at waist height, grip it, body straight from head to heels.
Pull your chest to the bar, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
mistakes: Not touching the bar with the chest

steps: Bar on the front of the shoulders, hands just outside them, glutes and abs tight.
Press the bar straight up, moving your head back then through once it passes.
Lower it back to the shoulders under control.
mistakes: Pressing the bar forward instead of up

steps: Sit with the back supported, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Press up until your arms are straight over your shoulders.
Lower back to shoulder height.
mistakes: Arching the lower back off the bench

steps: Start with the dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you.
Press up while rotating the palms to face forward.
Lower while rotating back to the start.
mistakes: Too heavy to control the turn

steps: Set the seat so the handles start at shoulder height.
Press up until the arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly to shoulder height.
mistakes: Locking the elbows hard at the top

steps: Stand with the dumbbells at your sides, slight bend in the elbows.
Raise them out to the sides up to shoulder height, leading with the elbows.
Lower slowly.
Stand side-on to a low pulley, handle in the far hand.
Raise the arm out to the side up to shoulder height.
Lower slowly, keeping tension on the cable.
mistakes: Raising above shoulder height with a shrug

steps: Stand with the dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Raise them in front of you to shoulder height with straight arms.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Going much higher than the shoulders

steps: Hinge forward with a flat back, dumbbells under the chest.
Raise them out to the sides with slightly bent elbows.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Squeezing the shoulder blades (it becomes a row)

steps: Hold the bar with hands about shoulder-width apart.
Pull it up along the body to chest height, elbows leading.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Pulling higher than the chest with a sore shoulder
Narrow grip that pinches the shoulders

steps: Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides.
Lift the shoulders straight up toward the ears.
Hold a moment, then lower slowly.
Stand with the dumbbells at your sides, palms forward, elbows by your body.
Curl them up without moving the elbows forward.
Lower all the way to straight arms.
Hold the bar shoulder-width apart, palms up, elbows by your sides.
Curl it up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
Hold the dumbbells at your sides with palms facing each other.
Curl them up keeping that grip.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Rotating the wrists during the curl

steps: Lie back on a bench at about 45°, arms hanging straight down.
Curl the dumbbells up without moving the elbows forward.
Lower to a full stretch.
mistakes: Lifting the shoulders off the bench
Too heavy to reach full stretch

steps: Set the seat so your armpits are snug against the top of the pad.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to almost straight arms.
mistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad

steps: Stand facing a low pulley with the bar or handle in your hands.
Curl up keeping the elbows by your sides.
Lower slowly, keeping tension on the cable.
Stand facing a high pulley, elbows by your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are straight.
Let it rise until the forearms are about parallel to the floor.
mistakes: Leaning over the bar to push with body weight

steps: Hold the rope with elbows by your sides.
Push down and spread the rope ends apart at the bottom.
Let it rise slowly.
Lie on a bench with the bar over your shoulders, arms straight.
Bend only at the elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead.
Extend the arms back up.
mistakes: Moving the upper arms (it becomes a press)

steps: Hold a dumbbell overhead with both hands, elbows pointing up.
Lower it behind your head by bending the elbows.
Extend the arms back up.
Lie as for the bench press, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Lower the bar to your lower chest with elbows close to the body.
Press back up.
mistakes: Grip so narrow it hurts the wrists

steps: Hands on the edge of a bench behind you, legs out in front.
Lower by bending the elbows until the upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Push back up.
mistakes: Hips drifting away from the bench

steps: Bar on the upper back, feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Sit down between your heels, knees following the toes, chest up.
Stand up by pushing the floor away.
Bar on the front of the shoulders, elbows high.
Squat down keeping the torso upright.
Stand up leading with the elbows.
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell against your chest.
Squat down between your knees with the chest up.
Stand up through the whole foot.
Back flat on the pad, feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Push back up without locking the knees hard.
mistakes: Partial reps with too much weight

steps: Feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform, back flat on the seat.
Lower until your knees are about 90°, without the hips lifting.
Push back up without locking the knees.
mistakes: Lower back rolling off the seat at the bottom
Locking the knees at the top

steps: Stand with the bar at your hips, knees slightly bent.
Push the hips back and slide the bar down the legs with a flat back.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings, then stand up.
mistakes: Rounding the back to go lower
Bending the knees more and more (it becomes a deadlift)

steps: Set the pad on the front of the ankles and line the knee up with the pivot.
Straighten the legs fully.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Lifting the hips off the seat

steps: Lie face down with the pad just above your heels.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Lower slowly to almost straight legs.
mistakes: Lifting the hips off the bench

steps: Sit with the pad above your heels and the thigh pad snug.
Pull your heels down and back as far as you can.
Return slowly.
Step forward and lower until both knees are about 90°.
Push through the front heel to bring the back leg forward into the next step.
Keep the torso upright throughout.
Rear foot on a bench, front foot far enough forward to keep the heel down.
Lower straight down until the front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Push back up through the front heel.
mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench

steps: Balls of the feet on the edge of a step or platform.
Rise as high as you can on your toes.
Lower slowly until the heels drop below the step.
Sit with the pad on your thighs and the balls of the feet on the platform.
Raise the heels as high as you can.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
Upper back on a bench, bar over the hips, feet flat and shoulder-width apart.
Drive the hips up until the body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze the glutes, then lower.
mistakes: Over-arching the lower back at the top
Feet too far or too close

steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat near your glutes.
Push through the heels and lift the hips until the body is straight.
Squeeze, then lower.
mistakes: Arching the back instead of squeezing the glutes

steps: Strap a low pulley to your ankle and hold the machine for balance.
Kick the leg straight back, squeezing the glute.
Return slowly.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to kick higher

steps: Forearms under the shoulders, body straight from head to heels.
Tighten the abs and glutes.
Breathe normally and hold.
Lie on your side with the elbow under the shoulder.
Lift the hips until the body is in a straight line.
Hold without letting the hips drop.
mistakes: Rotating the chest toward the floor

steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, hands by your head.
Curl your shoulders off the floor by tightening the abs.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Coming all the way up (it becomes a sit-up)

steps: Kneel facing a high pulley, rope by your head.
Curl your torso down, bringing elbows toward the knees.
Return slowly.
mistakes: Sitting back on the heels instead of curling

steps: Hang from a bar with straight arms.
Raise the legs by curling the pelvis up, not just lifting the thighs.
Lower slowly without swinging.
Kneel with the wheel under your shoulders.
Roll forward slowly, keeping the abs tight and the back flat.
Pull back with the abs to the start.
mistakes: Rolling out further than you can control

steps: Start walking, then raise the speed gradually.
Run tall with relaxed shoulders, landing under your hips.
Slow down to a walk for the last minutes.
mistakes: Long strides that land on the heel far in front

steps: Strap your feet in, sit tall, arms straight.
Push with the legs first, then lean back slightly and pull the handle to your lower ribs.
Return in reverse: arms, body, then legs.
mistakes: Pulling with the arms before the legs push

steps: Set the saddle so the knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Keep the torso relaxed and pedal smoothly.
Change the resistance rather than bouncing in the saddle.
mistakes: Too little resistance at high speed
